================================================================================
MASTER PROMPT: COMPREHENSIVE END-TO-END PROJECT REPORT GENERATION
COURSE: DLMBPDDT02 – Design Thinking | IU International University of Applied Sciences
================================================================================

ACT AS A LEAD PRODUCT DESIGNER AND DESIGN THINKING METHODOLOGIST.

YOUR TASK: Write a comprehensive, high-quality, end-to-end Project Report for the course "DLMBPDDT02 – Design Thinking" at IU International University of Applied Sciences. The target core text length is 12–15 pages (Master Level requirement), approx. 4,000 to 5,000 words of core body content (excluding preliminary pages, tables/lists, references, and appendices).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. SPECIFICATIONS, UNIVERSITY GUIDELINES & INSTRUCTOR REQUIREMENTS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The generation MUST strictly comply with all official IU examination and instructor guidelines:

A. CORE NATURE & DELIVERABLE SPECIFICATIONS:
   - PRODUCT DEVELOPMENT FOCUS: The project report is an evidence-based record of creating a concrete product/prototype ("MindfulFeed" social media app).
   - "NO RESEARCH ESSAY" MANDATE: It MUST NOT read like a traditional academic term paper, research essay, or consulting report. If it resembles a literature essay or theoretical paper, it fails.
   - EVIDENCE REQUIREMENT: The text must describe step-by-step practical execution, supported by explicit mockups, interview quotes, empathy maps, low/mid/hi-fi prototype iterations, usability testing grids, and feature matrices.
   - MARKET STRATEGY EXCLUSION: Focus strictly on product design, user research, and iterative development; market promotion or sales strategies are NOT required.

B. FORMAL FORMATTING STANDARDS:
   - CORE LENGTH: 12–15 pages of main body text (Master Level). Additional evidence (surveys, raw data, screen mockups) can be referenced for the appendix.
   - PERSPECTIVE & STYLE: Formal academic third-person perspective ONLY (avoid "I", "we", or "my"; use "the project team observed", "the design phase demonstrated"). Factual, precise, non-colloquial language.
   - HEADING LEVELS: Maximum of 3 heading levels (1. Heading, 1.1 Section, 1.1.1 Subheading).
   - PAGE NUMBERING LOGIC: Roman numerals (I, II, III...) for preliminary pages (TOC, Lists); Arabic numbers (1, 2, 3...) starting from Page 1 of the Introduction through the end.
   - MANDATORY COMPONENTS (In Order):
     1. Title Page
     2. Table of Contents
     3. List of Figures & List of Tables
     4. List of Abbreviations
     5. Core Text (Introduction ~10-15%, Main Body ~70-80%, Conclusion ~10-15%)
     6. Reference List (APA Style)
     7. Appendices / Generated Data Disclosures

C. GENERATIVE AI & PLAGIARISM GUIDELINES:
   - CITE AI USAGE: Transparently document and cite where GenAI tools were utilized for data simulation, user response modeling, or graphic concepts.
   - PROMPT DISCLOSURE: Include a short rationale for why AI tools were used (e.g., simulating qualitative user feedback loops across diverse demographics).
   - PLAGIARISM SAFETY: Generated content must be completely original to ensure near-zero similarity scores on Turnitin.

D. EVALUATION CRITERIA WEIGHTING:
   - Quality (25%): Analytical depth, logical coherence, and thorough reflection.
   - Process (25%): Coherence and adherence to the selected d.School Design Thinking stages.
   - Transfer (15%): Application of theory to practical problem-solving.
   - Creativity (15%): Originality in problem framing, ideation, and iterative refinement.
   - Documentation (10%): Academic style, structure, and formal criteria.
   - Resources (10%): Selection and efficient application of DT tools and resources.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. PROJECT TOPIC & SCOPE
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- PRODUCT NAME: "MindfulFeed" (A Pro-Social Social Media Application).
- PROJECT VISION: Build a pro-social, non-addictive social media application ("MindfulFeed") that actively replaces engagement-hacking dark patterns (infinite scroll, auto-playing feeds, variable rewards, outrage loops) with intentional user controls, finite content batching, ethical recommendation algorithms, and cognitive health safeguards.
- REGULATORY & THEORETICAL ANCHORS: Behavioral Economics (Choice Architecture / Thaler & Sunstein, 2008), Dark Pattern Taxonomies (Mathur et al., 2019; Mildner et al., 2023), Self-Determination Theory (Deci & Ryan, 2000), and EU Legal Standards (Digital Services Act & EU Digital Fairness Act Q4 2026).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. METHODOLOGY: TASK 2 – STANFORD d.SCHOOL 5-STAGE MODEL
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The main body must strictly follow the 5 sequential phases of the Stanford d.School approach:

1. EMPATHIZE: Qualitative study on digital burnout and platform harm. Must include:
   - Structured "User Interview Summary Table" with 3 distinct user profiles (raw quotes, addictive triggers, emotional impacts).
   - Complete Empathy Map Matrix (Says, Thinks, Does, Feels).
2. DEFINE: Synthesis of primary empirical findings. Must include:
   - Detailed Primary User Persona (Maya Lin).
   - Explicit Point of View (POV) Statement.
   - 3–4 strategic "How Might We" (HMW) Questions.
3. IDEATE: Structured solution generation. Must include:
   - Applied ideation tools (SCAMPER, Brainstorming).
   - Desirability, Feasibility, and Profitability (DFP) Filtering Matrix.
4. PROTOTYPE: Step-by-step physical/digital evolution across 3 distinct versions:
   - Version 1 (Low-Fi Paper Wireframe): Finite content batches and stopping cues.
   - Version 2 (Mid-Fi Digital UI): Pro-Social Algorithm Control Dashboard.
   - Version 3 (High-Fi Interactive Architecture): Complete pro-social feed, subscriber loops, and Ethical AI Compliance Indicator.
5. TEST: Empirical user validation for EACH prototype iteration. Must include:
   - "Feedback & Redesign Summary Table" detailing testing setups, user critiques, and direct redesign changes between v1, v2, and v3.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. DETAILED SECTION-BY-SECTION STRUCTURE & CONTENT SPECIFICATIONS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

PRELIMINARY PAGES (Numbered in Roman Numerals I, II, III...)
- Title Page
- Table of Contents
- List of Figures / List of Tables / List of Abbreviations

CORE TEXT (Numbered in Arabic Numerals 1, 2, 3...)

1. INTRODUCTION: PROJECT OBJECTIVES AND PREPARATIONS (~1.5–2 Pages | 10–15%)
   1.1 Context & Motivation:
       - Detail the systemic crisis of engagement-maximizing algorithms (infinite scroll, pull-to-refresh, auto-play queues, outrage loops).
       - Frame the legislative context of the EU Digital Services Act (DSA) and the EU Digital Fairness Act (targeted Q4 2026) banning addictive dark patterns.
   1.2 Product Vision & Scope:
       - Define "MindfulFeed" as an enterprise-grade pro-social app replacing engagement hacking with user autonomy.
       - Outline core product boundaries: finite content batching, explicit algorithm toggles, intentional friction nudges, and freemium/subscription value loops.
   1.3 Methodology Rationale:
       - Compare framework models in a structured comparison table: Stanford d.School (Selected) vs. IDEO Field Guide (Rejected for lacking a distinct Define phase) vs. HPI Micro-Cycle (Rejected for operational redundancy in software prototyping).
   1.4 Preparatory Work, AI Tools & Timeline:
       - Outline secondary research (UI audits, DSA/DFA regulatory texts, burnout studies).
       - Disclose GenAI application (simulating qualitative feedback loops across demographics).
       - Provide an ASCII text-based Project Execution Timeline diagram covering Weeks 1–8 across all 5 d.School phases.

2. MAIN BODY: IMPLEMENTATION, EVALUATION, AND REFLECTION (~9–11 Pages | 70–80%)
   2.1 Phase 1: Empathize
       - Qualitative research methodology on target user demographics.
       - Detailed "User Interview Summary Table" featuring 3 profiles:
         * User 1: Alex (Gen-Z Student) – Addictive triggers: Infinite scroll & auto-play; Impact: Sleep procrastination & cognitive fatigue.
         * User 2: Elena (Remote Analyst) – Addictive triggers: Outrage algorithms & notification loops; Impact: Attention fragmentation & workplace stress.
         * User 3: Marcus (Product Manager) – Addictive triggers: Pull-to-refresh dark patterns; Impact: Frustration over lost autonomy.
       - Complete "Empathy Map Matrix" synthesized across 4 quadrants: Says, Thinks, Does, Feels.
   2.2 Phase 2: Define
       - Primary User Persona: Maya Lin (26, UX Researcher/Hybrid Worker) detailing Demographics, Psychographics, Core Goals, and Frustrations with dark patterns.
       - Point of View (POV) Statement: Frame Maya's need for intentional engagement without falling victim to addictive loops.
       - Strategic "How Might We" (HMW) Questions: 3–4 questions bridging dark-pattern harm to tangible pro-social features (finite feeds, algorithm controls, non-addictive business models).
   2.3 Phase 3: Ideate
       - Document SCAMPER and Brainstorming ideation exercises.
       - Generate the "Desirability, Feasibility, and Profitability (DFP) Selection Matrix" evaluating 5 core concepts (Finite Batch Feeds, Intentional Friction, Algorithm Dashboard, Total Ad Prohibition, Hard Time Locks) and justifying adopted vs. rejected features.
   2.4 Phase 4 & Phase 5: Prototype & Test (Iterative Product Design Cycles)
       - Cycle 1 (Low-Fi Paper Wireframe & Testing): Focus on replacing infinite scroll with a 10-post "Batch Feed" and "Content Completion Marker". Detail usability testing feedback (stopping prompt felt too abrupt) and key learnings.
       - Cycle 2 (Mid-Fi Digital UI & Testing): Focus on interactive screen layouts for a "Pro-Social Algorithm Control Dashboard" (feed intent sliders, engagement toggles). Detail usability testing feedback (numerical sliders created cognitive overload) and key learnings (transition to preset intent modes).
       - Cycle 3 (High-Fi Interactive Architecture & Testing): Focus on full app execution featuring Finite Content Batches, Preset Mode Selectors ("Focus", "Discovery", "Social"), an Ethical AI Compliance Indicator (0% Dark Patterns), and Subscription Loops.
       - Integrated "Feedback & Redesign Summary Table": Map the exact progression of Feed Scrolling, Algorithm Adjustments, and Monetization Realism across Prototypes v1, v2, and v3.
   2.5 Strategic Product Evaluation & Reflection:
       - Balanced evaluation through Desirability (mental well-being), Feasibility (UI component design & rules-based AI logic), and Profitability (hybrid freemium/subscription monetization replacing ad-based dark patterns).
       - Reflection on practical experience using Design Thinking to solve complex software ethics.
       - Anchoring MindfulFeed into long-term user routines and market standards.

3. CONCLUSION: EVALUATION AND ANCHORING (~1.5–2 Pages | 10–15%)
   3.1 Synthesis of Results: Summary of how d.School phases translated theory and legal regulations into a functional, non-addictive application.
   3.2 Critical Reflection on Methodology: Evaluation of d.School strengths and limitations when applied to backend recommendation algorithms.
   3.3 Outlook for Future Practice: Perspective on ethical product design shifting from marketing differentiation to a regulatory necessity under the EU Digital Fairness Act.

POST-TEXT PAGES
- Reference List (APA Style)
- Appendix & GenAI Usage Disclosures (Prompts, reasoning, and raw simulation logs)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. RECOMMENDED GENERATION WORKFLOW
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
To ensure the generation tool produces all 12–15 pages without skipping details or truncating tables, feed the prompt in 3 sequential steps:

STEP 1:
"Paste the complete Master Prompt above. Execute the PRELIMINARY PAGES and SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION (~1.5–2 pages) with maximum academic detail."

STEP 2:
"Execute SECTION 2: MAIN BODY (~9–11 pages). Fully write out all interview tables, empathy maps, personas, DFP ideation matrices, and the 3 complete Prototype & Testing iteration cycles with the Feedback & Redesign Summary Table."

STEP 3:
"Execute SECTION 3: CONCLUSION (~1.5–2 pages), the APA REFERENCE LIST, and the APPENDIX WITH GEN-AI DISCLOSURES."
================================================================================
